chapter: New York arrival, Billy Hicks and the Black Cat
title: Skeets Talbot band members and the Black Cat sit-ins
summary: Personnel, nightly guests such as Goodman, Lester Young and Basie men, and the seven-night schedule.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Now, who was in the Skeets Talbot band?

Carl 'Taddy' Smith, who had been with Basie. The rest of the guys you wouldn't know, Lem Johnson was the tenor player. Freddy Jefferson was the piano player and Charles Bloomer was the drummer, who-he and I joined Benny Goodman on the Camel Caravan show in '39. Skeets Talbot was the alto and the arranger. He's a professor in Texas. That was it.
But every night, John would bring a different group of people down and they would sit in.

Benny Goodman and Lester Young had a battle of music that we played 'Honeysuckle Rose' for 45 minutes and in the interchange Lester played his clarinet and Benny played his tenor and the music hadn't been going for 45 minutes at that particular time. That was fantastic.

And Herschel Evans and Hersch Levins was there. Buck Clayton. Walter Page -- The drummer, [with] Woody Herman -- Dave Tough. Joe Jones. All these kind of people used to come down every night and they had a big furnace downstairs, we'd go downstairs and turn on, learn how to smoke pot. But it was fantastic but from seven to four, seven nights a week.
How long were the sets usually. When you didn't have someone sitting in in that situation where it might -- like 45 minutes sets and 15 off.

Oh, no, this was a specialty then. This was like a show. This was the show thing, but we had a show, we had people performing, you know, the regular routine. But when these guests came, they prevailed.
